solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Happening to team up after university in the end

indicators.note: after places the joining-forces word behind the university letter in the build

parts.note: a happening is an event, an occurrence
to ally is to join forces or team up

explanation.surface: Someone describes joining forces with a partner once their studies at university are finally over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean finally, after some time has passed.

clue.text: They've Ring cycles here — the whole lot

indicators.note: cycles suggests the letters going round and round into a new order

explanation.surface: A boast that Wagner's Ring cycle operas are all staged at this venue, the complete set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring cycles' points to Wagner's four-opera Ring cycle, but 'cycles' is the anagram signal working on the letters of THEYVE RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: all things, every single item, is the entire lot.

clue.text: Munch? European artist that's empty

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Edvard Munch, a European painter, is described as hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Munch looks like the Norwegian painter of The Scream, a natural partner for 'European artist'; the question mark signals it is the verb meaning chew.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to chew and swallow food noisily, a kind of consuming.

clue.text: Farm vehicle in large area of land corn's filling

parts.note: a tract is a large expanse of land

indicators.note: the filling of the word corn is its middle, everything inside its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tractor works in a big field with corn growing all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is just a link here: the corn's filling comes after the land, not inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the powerful vehicle used for pulling ploughs and machinery on farms.

clue.text: Not being awake as former prime minister stood up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s

explanation.surface: A sleepy observer notes that an ex-premier has risen to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' reverses the prime minister. Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister, founder of the modern police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is in a state of not being awake.

clue.text: Volume from Marvell I treasure

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a book of the poet Andrew Marvell's work as a personal treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book of Marvell's poems; it is a unit of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit measuring volume or capacity.

clue.text: Consenting to nothing yet being paid?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, all of a sum is still owed, so none has been paid

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to an arrangement even though they haven't received a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ALL OWING, the second definition says every bit of the debt is still outstanding; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitting something is a form of agreeing to it, a synonym for consenting.

clue.text: Run for someone to play a small part

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored without the batter hitting it, such as a wide or bye

definitions.text: someone to play a small part
definitions.meaning: a film actor with a tiny non-speaking role, as in a crowd scene

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in a minor role in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run added to the total that is not credited to a batter, such as a wide or a bye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a bonus cricket score and a background film actor.

clue.text: Short title reset on line

indicators.note: to reset type is to set it again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A brief heading is retypeset onto a single line of print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' rearranges TITLE together with L for line, 'on' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small in stature or length; a short person is a little one.

clue.text: Pedant upset with term for division

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fussy stickler is annoyed by a word used to describe a division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' acts on PEDANT and TERM together, 'with' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section or branch of an organisation, a division of it.

clue.text: Agreement to finish every clue thus?

indicators.note: the finish of each of the next three words is its final letter

explanation.surface: A setter asks whether every crossword clue should end the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'every', 'clue' and 'thus' are Y, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the affirmative word signals assent or agreement.

clue.text: A light meal somewhere in Kent

definitions.meaning: a snack of filling between two slices of bread
a historic town and port in Kent, south-east England

explanation.surface: A snack is taken somewhere in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a small town in Kent, a county in south-east England; the Earl of Sandwich is said to have given his title to the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread snack is a light meal, and the name is also an English town.

clue.text: And so the referee gets more, but not millions

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove a letter from the word just named

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: A referee is paid more money, though not millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not millions' takes M from MORE, leaving ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are connectives introducing a consequence: for that reason, hence.

clue.text: Country with no area lacking food

indicators.note: with no means the letter for area is removed

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A country short of space is described as being without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no area' drops A from HUNGARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without food leaves you wanting to eat, the state of starving.

clue.text: A short day getting about continent

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviated form of Friday
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A brief day trip around a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, Latin for about, used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is one of the world's seven great landmasses.

clue.text: Chemical recipe representing alum turned up

parts.note: for can mean on behalf of, representing

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A chemical formula stands for alum, a compound that has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses alum, which reads upwards in a down clue; alum is itself a chemical, adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's formula sets out the ingredients and proportions, like a recipe.

clue.text: A quiet set of bells offers a certain attraction

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a peal is a set of tuned church bells

explanation.surface: A softly ringing set of church bells has a particular charm.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the musical term for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is the quality of attracting interest, a synonym for allure.

clue.text: Breasts come back in more recent daily

indicators.note: in puts the turned breasts word inside the more-recent word
come back means the word for breasts is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: paps is an old word for breasts or nipples

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about bosoms making a return in a newer edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come back' reverses the old word for breasts; 'daily' is a noun, a paper published each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every weekday, a common noun use.

clue.text: Arrange to include one manifest

indicators.note: to include means the word for arrange holds the numeral one inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Organise things so that one obvious item is included.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean obvious, clear to see.

clue.text: Had ghosts appearing regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of ghosts

explanation.surface: Someone was haunted by ghosts that turned up on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'ghosts' are G, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tense forms meaning possessed or obtained.

clue.text: Write off English predicament

parts.note: to scrap something is to write it off

explanation.surface: An English car crash leaves a vehicle written off and its owner in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky situation one has got into, an awkward fix.

clue.text: Punt, not the first that is set free

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of punt is dropped

parts.note: ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A flat-bottomed boat that isn't the leading one is released from its moorings.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is a flat river boat pushed with a pole, as on the Cam at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or binding is to release or liberate something.

clue.text: Meal of duck cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a teal is a small freshwater duck

explanation.surface: A dinner of roast duck is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be an evening or late-afternoon meal, not just a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage it names a light afternoon or evening repast.

clue.text: Awfully pale suntan is not very nice

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking holiday tan is far from attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' looks like an intensifier for 'pale'; it rearranges PALE SUNTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeable or nasty, the opposite of pleasant.
